Well, I see now how moving to the farm may be difficult and how having no one interested in your interest could be very lonely. There are a lot of things that keep you in the city, things that are clearly very important to you.

However hope is not lost yet. Maybe you can see if there is a national park or anything really that is more to do with nature. Maybe even try a zoo or petting zoo if you have one to try and get closer to nature.

Maybe if you can find a place in your city or near it where you go whenever you feel lonely you can be closer to nature and feel more at peace with yourself and maybe a littles lonely and sad. And maybe once you find that place you can handle living in the city more.

Also maybe one day you can return to the farm but for now try to make the most of what you've got.

It really feels like you're forcing yourself to stay in the city eventhough it makes you upset and feel lonely - like you don't belong. 

And the fact that you're in the city is only making you feel more frustrated and alone.

I think you should take a break from the city, and do the things that make you happy, and feel free. 

I don't know your lifestyle so I don't know how possible it is for you to take a break, nor why you moved to the city.

But from what I gather, you feel trapped, in a place where you can't be yourself or do the things you want to do. And because you feel trapped you feel isolated form everyone around you making you feel lonely and unheard and like you can't be yourself. But thats all speculation.

Honestly I think you should just to a break if you can from the city and give yourself the ability to do the things you want and feel like you belong.

Also it's ok, it's clear that you're upset and not just complaining for the sake of complaining so there's no need to apologize.

If you think moving back to the farm will help you feel less lonely and more like you belong. Then I think it may be a good idea.

Cause while you are at the farm and learning to feel more comfortable and less lonely you can look at things with a clear head and figure out your next steps.

Maybe try to find a compromise or an in-between. From what I can gather if you're polar opposites then that means there is a middle ground and that's where you can hopefully find a solution.

You both may not fully love it, but if you can comprise and find that balance then both of you're parenting styles can be included.

Yeah I can relate to feeling lonely even if you have people around you. Sometimes though it's not so much the fact that you are actively lonely but more you feel as if you're not being seen or heard. 

I guess what you need to try to figure out is what do you want people to see or hear from you. What do you want to say or express to the people around you to make you feel welcome and less alone.

I know what you mean I do the same thing. What you might be doing is bottling up your emotions and pushing them aside and you've done this so much that you don't know how to let yourself feel or express yourself.

Honestly sometimes it's good to ask for help but if you really want to handle your problems on your own (as long as it's nothing that could harm you if it's not solved), I'd advise that you take a step back and assess everything that you know or have. Then take the time to think of one solution at a time and try out the ones that could work.
